column1: # stateful-global-regex triage ledger — judged `.test()`/`.exec()` sites whose
# receiver is a MODULE-LEVEL regex bearing the `g` (or `y`) flag.
# STATUS: SAFE (lastIndex is managed — reset before use, or a drain-to-null loop
#         that self-resets) | BUG (open: a bare .test()/.exec() on a persistent
#         /g regex with no reset and no full drain — intermittent wrong answer).
# The question for each site: across repeated calls, can this regex's lastIndex
# carry a nonzero cursor INTO this call? A `re.lastIndex = 0` immediately before,
# or a `while ((m = re.exec(x)) !== null)` loop that always runs to null (which
# resets the cursor), makes it safe. A single .test()/.exec() with neither is the
# bug. Add a row here only after judging WHY a site is safe (or fixing it).
# Key = whitespace-collapsed snippet, so it survives reformatting / line shifts.
